title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-243t: TH_2 uses raw concatenation instead of CBOR Sequence per RFC 9528
description:
## Bug: TH_2 hash input encoding violates RFC 9528

### Location
`lichen/subsys/lichen/edhoc/edhoc.c`, lines 720-723 (initiator) and 1161-1164 (responder)

### Current code
```c
uint8_t th2_input[64];  /* 32 (G_Y) + 32 (H(message_1)) */
memcpy(th2_input, ctx->g_y, 32);
memcpy(th2_input + 32, h_msg1, 32);
ret = sha256_hash(th2_input, 64, ctx->th_2);
```

### RFC 9528 Section 4.1.2 requirement
"Compute the transcript hash TH_2 = H( G_Y, H(message_1) ), where H() is the EDHOC hash algorithm of the selected cipher suite. **The input to the hash function is a CBOR Sequence.**"

### Problem
The code does raw concatenation: `G_Y(32) || H(message_1)(32)` = 64 bytes.

CBOR sequence requires each item individually CBOR-encoded as a bstr:
- `bstr(G_Y)`: 0x58 0x20 + 32 bytes = 34 bytes
- `bstr(H(message_1))`: 0x58 0x20 + 32 bytes = 34 bytes
- Total: 68 bytes

The `compute_th()` helper already does this correctly (zcbor_bstr_encode_ptr for each input). TH_2 should use `compute_th()` or manually encode the CBOR bstr headers.

### Impact
P0: Produces wrong TH_2 value. Cascades to PRK_2e, KEYSTREAM_2, TH_3, TH_4, and all derived keys (PRK_out, OSCORE keys). Implementation will not interoperate with any other RFC 9528-conformant implementation.

### Fix
Use `compute_th(ctx->th_2, ctx->g_y, 32, h_msg1, 32, NULL, 0)` in both initiator and responder paths, or add explicit zcbor_bstr_encode for the two inputs.
